small_guidance:
- The kernel does 4× tl.dot per K-tile (one per pooling cell) but reloads input at 4 nearby offsets; try larger BLOCK_M (e.g., 128) with BLOCK_N=32 to increase OC reuse since BLOCK_N=64 means 64 pooling positions × 4 cells = 256 output columns per program — adding configs like (BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=32, BLOCK_K=32, num_warps=8) and (BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=32, num_warps=8, num_stages=3) may help.
- Swap the grid order so pid_sp varies fastest within an SM (program_id(1)=sp, program_id(2)=oc) to improve L2 locality on weights across spatial tiles sharing the same OC tile.
- Cache weight tile once and reuse across the 4 dots (already done implicitly), but consider hoisting bias/SUB combination and pre-subtracting SUB from bias on host to remove the `- SUB` from the epilogue.
large_guidance:
- Switch to a channels-last (NHWC) input layout so the GEMM-K dimension (IC*KH*KW) is contiguous along IC; this lets the K-loop do coalesced vector loads instead of strided gather per (kh,kw,ic) and typically gives 1.5-2× on conv-as-GEMM at these sizes.
- Restructure as one program per (N, OC tile, pooled-spatial tile) that directly accumulates the 2×2 conv outputs into a single max via online reduction, but use a BLOCK_N covering pooled positions where each thread handles its own 2×2 window with shared weight tiles — reduces 4 separate accumulator matrices to a single running-max accumulator, halving register pressure and enabling larger BLOCK_M.
- Consider implicit-GEMM with weight pre-packed as [OC, IC*KH*KW] in shared memory once per OC tile (persistent kernel across spatial tiles for the same (n, oc)), amortizing the weight load across all pooled-spatial tiles for that (n, oc).
